Hi Elena / Audrey,

Thanks again for joining the demo today — appreciate the thoughtful questions. Per our conversation I wanted to capture the open items on data handling and access controls so your security and legal teams can review and we can qualify next steps. I've attached a short support-access matrix to show roles, break-glass flow, and typical audit trails.

Quick summary of asks from your side:
- Confirm whether Finido treats usernames + email as PII and whether hashed/email redaction is required at rest.
- Retention policy for call/interaction logs: how long do you require query logs and full request payloads be retained?
- Acceptable support access model: ephemeral role elevation vs. full-support account.
- Data residency preference (US/EU) for model activation and persisted artifacts.

Next steps I propose:
1) Our security lead (Jonas) will reply with the default platform behavior and options for stricter controls.
2) We'll attach a short SOC2 excerpt and the support matrix.
3) If helpful, schedule a 30-min call between your security lead and Jonas to confirm break-glass telemetry and auditability.

Attachments: support-access-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet, 42KB)

If there are additional stakeholders who should be on the follow-up (legal, infra), please loop them in — otherwise, we'll wait for your prioritization and proposed times.

Subject: Re: Post-demo: Customer data access, PII handling & break-glass questions

Thanks Neha — good recap. A few clarifying points from our end:

1) For Finido, email addresses and full names are considered PII. We prefer server-side redaction or hashing on read for exported logs. Can Redwood support an opt-in redaction step before logs are persisted?

2) Retention: our default requirement is 90 days for request/response logs (for troubleshooting) and 365 days for auth/audit trails. Is that configurable per-tenant?

3) Support access: we require least-privilege escalation that is time-bound and requires approval from our security admin. If you have an auditable break-glass workflow that logs approver, reason, and session replay hashes, that would satisfy our auditors.

4) Residency: We prefer US for now but need the option to pin to EU within 60 days if we expand there.

Can you also send your SOC2 excerpt and an example of the audit trail fields we can expect from a break-glass event? I'm including Audrey (our Head of Infrastructure). We'll likely schedule the security call next week.

Best,
Elena

Neha / team — putting together concise answers to share back with Finido. Notes below are our recommended defaults and options we can offer. I copied Vanessa and Marissa for contract and CS context.

1) PII handling- Default: Redwood does not persist raw request payloads beyond configured retention. Customers can enable "PII redaction" which performs deterministic hashing of specified fields (email, ssn, name) prior to persistence. Offer: we can provide a custom redaction hook to run prior to logging if Finido wants additional transforms.

2) Retention- Default logs retention: 30 days for full request/response payloads; 365 days for auth & audit logs. Configurable per-tenant at onboarding with higher retention tiers for dedicated/private deployments. For hosted customers we support contract-level retention SLAs (90 / 365 / custom).

3) Support access & break-glass- Model: least-privilege ephemeral elevation. Flow: support engineer requests session elevation -> customer security admin receives approval email (or auto-approve based on prior SSO token) -> system issues time-limited credential (~30min) tied to support session id -> all commands are recorded and stored in audit log. Audit fields: session_id, requester_id, approver_id, reason, start_ts, end_ts, actions_summary (operation hashes). We retain a signed transcript and a replay-hash for tamper-evidence. We also emit an event to customer webhook for near‑real-time alerting.

4) Data residency- We support region pinning for inference and persistence. For hosted customers we can pin to US or EU regions at onboarding; for private deployments we support on-prem/air‑gapped. Migration path: we can provision EU tenancy in ~6-8 weeks with data-migration assistance.

Attached: SOC2-excerpt.pdf (controls summary; redactions removed) and a one-page example of the audit log schema. Suggested next step: Neha to propose a 30-min security sync next week (Jonas + Audry/Finido sec).

Regards,
Jonas

Elena/Audrey — thanks for the quick follow. Summary below and proposed times.

Summary answers (short)
- PII: Yes, emails & full names are considered PII. We offer per-tenant PII redaction (deterministic hashing) prior to persistence; custom hooks are available for enterprise/private.
- Retention: Configurable. Hosted default is 30d for payloads / 365d for auth/audit; we can offer 90d payload retention at contract level.
- Support access: Ephemeral role elevation with approver, reason, session_id, start/end timestamps, action hashes. All actions recorded and tamper-evident.
- Residency: We can pin to US now; EU pinning available with provisioning lead time.

Attachments included: support-access-matrix.xlsx, SOC2-excerpt.pdf

- Tue 24 Mar 10:00-10:30 PT
- Wed 25 Mar 14:00-14:30 PT

If one of those works for Audrey or your security admin, I'll send a calendar invite and add Jonas. Also let us know whether Finido wants the 90d payload retention option in a draft SOW so Marissa can include pricing.

Thanks — happy to iterate on any of the controls.
